speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your issue, could you please tell me which ear was operated on and how long ago your tympanoplasty was performed? Also, is the shooting pain constant or does it only occur when pressure is applied to the earlobe?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any numbness or tingling sensations in the area around your right ear or jaw, and does the shooting pain worsen specifically when you chew or move your jaw? I also need to know if there is any visible redness, swelling, or discharge at the earring piercing sites to rule out infection or contact dermatitis.

text: Does the pain radiate to your jaw or temple, and have you noticed any tenderness when I press on the tragus of your ear? I also need to check if there is any inflammation or crusting at the earring sites to rule out contact dermatitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient's denial of facial tenderness and jaw clicking makes temporomandibular joint dysfunction less likely. Since the pain is triggered by eating and the ear exam is normal, I suspect referred pain from the trigeminal nerve or dental issues. Do you have any dental pain, gum swelling, or sensitivity in your right upper teeth, and does the pain feel like an electric shock?
